subjects.displayTitle: The Greatest Name: remembrance, recognition, and renewal
subjects.introduction: One pilgrim remembered, decades later, the joy that overcame him when his eyes fell on the Greatest Name hanging in a place of honour in a room. That memory is a good place to begin, because the Greatest Name is first of all something that happens to a person: a word on the lips at dawn, a refuge in trouble, the last breath before sleep. Bahá’u’lláh teaches that the Name is also a proclamation, the sun rising from the supreme horizon, the banner of pre-existence raised on the mount of the world, and that to remember it is to recognise the One it names. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanation of the ringstone symbol lays out the worlds of God, of command and of creation, with revelation as the mirror between them. The Qur’án’s invitation to call upon God by His most beautiful names gives this devotion an older setting [1]. From here the journey leads to Bahá’u’lláh Himself, to the daily recitation of the Name and the law of repetition that shapes a habit into a character, and to the Word of God and the power of speech, where a name becomes a life.
subjects.arc: Begin with joy and daily remembrance, explore meanings and symbols, follow the language of hidden and manifest revelation, then read prayers for renewal and the call to steadfast action.

order.why: Follow remembrance through waking, daily trouble, and rest.
shortened: The Greatest Name should be found upon the lips in the first awaking moment of early dawn. It should be fed upon by constant use in daily invocation, in trouble, under opposition, and should be the last word breathed when the head rests upon the pillow at night.
It is the name of comfort, protection, happiness, illumination, love and unity.

order.why: Open with remembered joy at seeing the Greatest Name.
shortened: When my gaze fell upon the Greatest Name, occupying as it did the place of honour in the room of this great personage, I was all at once overcome by a feeling of immense joy and happiness. To this day the memory of that joy and happiness abideth with me; nor shall I ever forget it."

order.why: Invite discovery of meanings within the invocation.
shortened: Give especial greeting to ... and say: "There lie glorious meanings in the word "Allaho-ABHA". I hope thou wilt discover those significances."

order.why: Read the sweetness of conscience in devotional imagery.
Hear the call that stirs the speaker’s spirit.
shortened: Yet in this Day the cry of the Concourse on high is "Allah-u-Abha," and the spirit of this servant is stirred and thrilled by this Call.

order.why: Keep greeting and invocation distinct in the source’s wording.
shortened: The greeting is the blessed word "Baha-u-Abha" which is inscribed by the Supreme Pen on the tablets of hearts, and the call and melody of the sanctified Concourse in the upper realm is "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha"!

order.why: Read the longing to hear the blessed Name from another’s tongue.
shortened: Due to the honor of this blessed Name, I long to see thy face so that I may hear this blessed Name from thy tongue with my own ears. Consider with what a bounty thou hast been distinguished!

order.why: Introduce the Name’s connection with the Blessed Beauty and its letters.
Clarifies the permissibility of displaying the Greatest Name.
Keep the commentary’s parallel explanation.
Read the ringstone’s three worlds and channel of grace.
Treat the symbol as an invitation to further understanding.
Connect the chain and keys to servitude.
shortened: The chain of servitude to the Blessed Beauty is connected to and associated with the Greatest Name, and the keys are an indication that this chain of servitude is the means of opening doors and is in every way a protection for the heart and soul and a safeguard for the spirit and mind.

order.why: Read the Night of Power and the letter H in the source’s symbolism.
shortened: We have adorned the Night of Power with the letter "H" that the people of Baha may attain certitude through this Most Great, Supreme Name.

order.why: Read the particular name Husayn within the stated symbolism.
Keep the interpretation of Revelation’s stars and spirits attributed.
Read the Point, B, and Alif in their symbolic language.
Consider the point of knowledge and the cited commentary.
Read the Bab’s fourfold account of the Most Great Name.
Hear the Bab’s expansive praise through divine names.
Preserve the opening praise from the Qayyumu’l-Asma’.
Consider revelation of the Name through the reference to the Torah.
Read the promise in the Books of God.
Keep the account of the Name inscribed in scriptures.
shortened: Say: O concourse of the world! By God, the Most Great Name hath come, which was inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen in every unfurled scroll, every sealed book, and every recorded tablet.

order.why: Read the claim concerning proof and evidence.
Consider the hidden key becoming manifest.
Read the concealed Name in prayer becoming speaking reality.
shortened: All have heard that it hath been said that the Most Great Name is mentioned and concealed in this prayer, and now it is manifest and speaking and hath dawned upon all who dwell on earth.

order.why: Keep the account of precedence at the opening of prayer.
Read the prayer’s opening with its source omission visible.
Consider the instruction to recite at dawn.
shortened: O my God and my Beloved! This is the Name wherewith Thou hast adorned the preamble of the Tablet of Eternity, and made it the ornament of Thine own Self, O Thou Who art the Sovereign of the kingdoms of names. And Thou hast commanded all to recite it at dawn, that none among those endowed with vision might be debarred therefrom.

order.why: Retain the acceptance of a compilation of verses about the Name.
shortened: That which thou hast extracted from the verses concerning the Greatest Name was accepted before the Throne.

order.why: Read the Name described as the One who speaks.
Keep the Ancient Beauty’s call and glad tidings.
shortened: The Ancient Beauty hath turned His face toward the world, and verily He is the Most Great Name, calling out with the most exalted call and bringing glad tidings to those in the kingdom of creation, unto God, the Sender of winds.

order.why: Consider the movement from silence to utterance.
shortened: O Most Great Name! We, verily, have made thee to be among the greatest of names, that thou mayest issue forth from the abode of silence, and rise above the dawning-place of utterance to proclaim a Cause that hath encompassed all worlds.

order.why: Read the direct announcement of the Lord of Eternity.
shortened: It crieth out by its own self and saith: "By God! The Lord of Eternity hath come with the Most Great Name.

order.why: Hear the call addressed to the peoples of the earth.
shortened: O peoples of the earth! The Most Great Name hath come, calling you unto the Supreme Horizon.

order.why: Keep the summons toward the highest horizon.
Read the Tablet’s proclamation.
Consider joy in the days of God.
shortened: The Tongue hath spoken before the faces of the world and given them glad tidings of the Most Great Name, that they might rejoice in the days of God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Keep the Spirit’s glad tidings and illumination.
shortened: The verses were sent down when the signs appeared and the Spirit speaketh between the world and giveth glad-tidings unto the nations of the Most Great Name, whereby all who are in the heavens and earth were illumined.

order.why: Read the call between earth and heaven.
Preserve the proclamation of the hidden Name’s manifestation.
Read illumination beside human failure to perceive.
shortened: The horizon of the world hath been illumined by the Sun of My Most Great Name, yet most of the people perceive not.

order.why: Keep the related appeal to true vision.
Consider the world’s adornment and heedlessness.
shortened: The world hath been adorned with the ornament of the Most Great Name, yet most of the people remain heedless.

order.why: Read the image of the world’s expanded breast.
Keep the sun rising from the supreme horizon.
shortened: The sun of My Most Glorious Name has dawned from the supreme horizon.

order.why: Read the raised banner of pre-existence.
shortened: The Banner of Pre-existence hath been raised through the Most Great Name upon the mount of the world. Blessed is he who hasteneth unto it with his heart.

order.why: Locate the Name within the description of this cycle.
Keep the affirmation of the world’s illumination.
shortened: Verily, Thou art the Lord of the world, the Almighty over the nations, and the One made manifest through the Most Great Name, whereby the heavens and earth were illumined in Thy wondrous and wonderful Day.

order.why: Read divine unity and the world’s new adornment.
Consider recognition in the passage on divine unity.
shortened: Say: The true believer in divine unity is he who cleaveth unto this Name which God hath made the Sovereign of Names, and he who turneth away from it remaineth veiled in concealment.

order.why: Read the Name as dayspring of names and attributes.
shortened: By God! Nothing that is witnessed and seen will profit you this Day save through this Name which God has made the Dayspring of His names, the Manifestation of His attributes and the Dawning-Place of His firm and mighty Cause.

order.why: Keep the recipient’s recognition and the ocean image.
shortened: This is an epistle from the All-Bestowing to him who hath believed in God, the Lord of Lords, and attained unto the Most Great Ocean when it surged through this Name which God hath made to prevail over all who are in the lands.

order.why: Read the wider setting of recognition and the Day of God.
Consider detachment and response to the Day.
shortened: All have been created for this Day, yet all are found to be heedless and veiled save those who have cast away the world and have clung to the Most Great Name, whereby the hearts of the peoples who turned away from God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, have been shaken.

order.why: Keep the imagery of scattering and gathering attributed.
Read the source’s language of opposition and dispersal.
Hear the invitation to take hold of the Name.
Keep the blessing of holding to the luminous hem.
Join detachment and a portion of grace.
Read the opened seal and choice wine imagery.
shortened: Hold fast unto My strong cord, then drink from the choice wine of My Most Glorious Name, whose seal We have broken through My sovereignty and power.

order.why: Consider pearls of knowledge and certitude.
Read the opening of mercy, knowledge, and understanding.
shortened: Today through the key of the Most Great Name the gates of bounty, mercy, compassion, knowledge and understanding have been opened before the faces of the world.

order.why: Join opening utterance to opening hearts.
shortened: We have opened the gates of utterance with the key of Our Most Great Name, and hearts through this Name whereby all who are in the heavens and on earth have been attracted - were We to speak of it, all would be thunderstruck.

order.why: Hear the call to remembrance as spiritual life.
shortened: Impart thou the Greatest Name to the ears, so that all may call out among nations: "O Thou Baha' of the world! O Thou Sun of Pre-existence!"
Truly, I say unto thee, this blessed Name is the spirit of life, the deliverer from death, the word of salvation and of manifest signs!

order.why: Read sight and life explicitly in their spiritual meanings.
Keep the concise invitation to renewed life.
Read the healing and quickening imagery in its devotional setting.
Join supplication to concern for the blind, captive, and deprived.
Consider love as the remedy described by the source.
Read the physician-of-hearts prayer and the remedy of knowledge.
shortened: O Physician of troubled hearts! For every chronic disease bestow the potent remedy of the Covenant, and for every incurable pain grant the instantaneous cure of divine knowledge, so that the power of the Most Great Name may influence both essence and form, bringing dead bones back to life though they be decomposed.

order.why: Keep the source omission in the account of spiritual rebirth.
Read the promised effects in soul and conscience as attributed.
Consider generosity embodied in revelation.
Keep the imagery of breezes stirring hearts.
Read the manifest bestowals as rays of sunlight.
shortened: O friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! Praise be to God, the bestowals of the Greatest Name are manifest like the rays of the sun, its radiance is evident, and all are present in His Kingdom.

order.why: Retain the brief affirmation of all-encompassing favors.
shortened: The favors of the Most Great Name are all-encompassing!

order.why: Hear the invitation to joy under providence.
Read the counsel about visible devotional reminders.
shortened: Thus if you desire protection from the powers of the world and earthly influences, place the Greatest Name in your dwelling, wear the ring of the Greatest Name, and keep Abdul Baha'is photograph in your home.

order.why: Keep the practical response to a request for stones.
Retain the reported joy at recognizing the inscription.
shortened: "Oh! Upon this stone is impressed the Name of Baha'u'llah" she fairly cried out with happiness and serenity in her face.

order.why: Keep the reported healing recollection and the speaker’s interpretation attributed.
shortened: I suggested some simple remedy, and he gave that along with the one he had been giving, I sat by the child and took its hand, and said the Greatest Name, and in a few hours the child began to improve. As far as my mentality goes I cannot see that the remedy did the child any good.

order.why: Enter the Bab’s invocation through the Name and revealed knowledge.
shortened: I invoke Thee by Thy Most Great Name through which the hidden secrets of God, the Most Exalted, were divulged and the kindreds of all nations converged toward the focal center of faith and certitude, through which Thy luminous Words streamed forth for the quickening of mankind and the essence of all knowledge was revealed from that Embodiment of bounty.

order.why: Read the prayer of divine unity.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name which hath spoken that there is no God but Thee, and Glory be unto Thee, O my God!

order.why: Ask for good in this world and the next.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy binding Command and by Thy Most Great Name, whereby the hearts of the nations were stirred, to ordain for me the good of this world and the next.

order.why: Keep the related prayer for the loved ones.
Join turning toward bounty to the tabernacle of wisdom.
shortened: I implore Thee, by Thy Most Great Name through Which Thou didst stir up Thy servants and build up Thy cities, and by Thy most excellent titles, and Thy most august attributes, to assist Thy people to turn in the direction of Thy manifold bounties, and set their faces towards the Tabernacle of Thy wisdom.

order.why: Read the Sinai imagery in the prayer for an opened door.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Him Who conversed upon Sinai, Who has ascended the throne of manifestation, and by the fire of Thy Sacred Tree, and by Thy Greatest Name whereby Thou hast subdued the cities of names, to open before my face the door of Thy bounty, Thy grace, Thy might and Thy wealth.

order.why: Hear the request for a tranquil heart and expanded breast.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Him Who is the Purpose of the world and by the Most Great Name which Thou hast manifested amidst the nations, and through Whose Most Exalted Pen Thou hast caused to flow the Kawthar of everlasting life, and through Whom Thou hast quickened whatsoever Thou didst purpose in the kingdom of creation, that Thou wilt send down from the heaven of Thy bounty and the clouds of Thy generosity that which will tranquilize my heart, gladden mine eyes and dilate my breast.

order.why: Keep the prayer for the loved ones’ gladness.
Join steadfastness with joy and tranquility.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Most Great Name, through which the Kingdom of Names appeared and all things came into being, to assist Thy loved ones to achieve the most great steadfastness, and to ordain for them, through Thy bounty and grace, that which will bring joy to their eyes,
tranquility to their souls, and gladness to their hearts.

order.why: Read the request for firmness in the Cause and love.
shortened: Say: O God of the world and Lord of the nations! I beseech Thee by the Most Great Name, through which the lands were shaken and the servants were disturbed, to make me steadfast in Thy Cause and firm in Thy love.

order.why: Keep the personal prayer for nearness and steadfastness.
shortened: O Siyyid Muhammad! Say: My God, my God! I beseech Thee by the lights of Thy throne and the manifestations of Thy power, and by the Lamp through which Thy dominion and Thy kingdom were illumined, and by Thy Most Great Name whereby the ocean of recognition surged before the faces of the peoples, to ordain for me that which will draw me nigh unto Thee and make me steadfast in Thy Cause - the Cause whereby the feet of the people of Thy realm have slipped.

order.why: Consider purification and drawing near.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name, through which Thou hast separated between the nations, that Thou send down from the clouds of Thy mercy that which will purify the people of Thy dominion, that they may draw near unto the Dayspring of Thy Revelation, the Dawning-Place of Thine inspiration, the Treasury of Thy knowledge, and the Repository of Thy Will.

order.why: Hear the handmaiden’s prayer for divine good-pleasure.
Read the prayer recalling detached handmaidens.
Keep grief, remembrance, and love together.
Retain the named servant Rida’s particular prayer.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great, Most Glorious Name, through which the ocean of bounty surged and the fragrance of eternity wafted, to assist Thy servant Rida in that which Thou lovest and approvest.

order.why: Read the prayer for one who recognized and served in the earliest days.
Keep longing for sacrifice in the prayer’s historical devotional voice.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Light of the world and Illuminator of the nations, by the Most Great Name, to ordain for me that which Thou hast destined for Thy chosen ones and trusted ones, who were so carried away by the breathings of Thy Revelation that they hastened to the place of sacrifice in their longing to attain Thy presence.

order.why: Ask for the portion of those who acknowledge the Prophets.
Hear the prayer for a child’s protection.
shortened: Thou seest a young child, the son of one who bears my name - upon him be my glory - clinging to Thy All-Bountiful Name and to Thy Most Great Name. I beseech Thee, O Lord of the worlds and Master of nations, by the Most Great Name, to protect him with the hosts of the unseen and the seen, and ordain for him what Thou hast ordained for Thy chosen ones and trusted ones.

order.why: Keep the extended prayer for protection and healing.
Read the prayer for the bearer of the white leaf.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Most Great Name, the All-Glorious, the Most Glorious, and by the Ultimate Tree, the Most Exalted, the All-Exalted, that Thou protect the bearer of this white leaf from all evil, calamity, plague and pestilence.

order.why: Retain the prayer’s protective imagery and request for steadfastness.
Read the prayer for protection amid opposition.
Join remembrance of a martyr to bounty for all peoples.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Him Whom Thou didst name 'Ali in Thy Book, who was martyred in Thy path in the Land of Ya, to open through the key of Thy Most Great Name the doors of Thy grace and bounty unto all peoples.

order.why: Keep the opening of gates through the Name.
Hear the prayer to give voice to remembrance.
Read thanksgiving and praise as a public utterance.
shortened: O truthful speaker, it behooves you to extend the hands of thanksgiving and praise toward the Divine Presence and say: Praise be unto You, O Quickener of moldering bones, Educator of nations, and the One Who has dawned upon the horizons of the world through the Greatest Name, for having guided me to the bright pathway and the easy, exemplary road wherein there is neither crookedness nor decline, and for causing me to speak Your mention among humanity until I cry out with the loudest call: "Glory and sanctity belong to the Lord of the highest heavens!

order.why: Join love, speaking the Name, and the prayer not to be left to oneself.
shortened: Be thou known for thy love of thy Lord and for giving voice to this Great Name.

Convey My remembrance unto thy brother, saying: Turn with thy most pure heart to the Most Great Scene and say: "O Lord of mankind! I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name not to leave me to myself, and to make me ever-mindful of Thee, detached from all creation.

order.why: Retain the particular recipient’s remembrance.
Read the words as fragrances of the All-Merciful.
shortened: Thus have We wafted unto thee the fragrances of the All-Merciful from this Paradise, and verily thou shalt find them in My most wondrous and matchless words.

order.why: Consider the atoms’ testimony in the poetic address.
Keep the Book’s speaking and the hearer’s response.
shortened: Verily the Book speaketh through this Most Great Name, whereby the hearts of the world were shaken, save those who heard the Call and said: "Here am I, O Lord of the verses!

order.why: Prepare inward hearing through detachment from desire.
Read the conquest of hearts through wise remembrance.
Keep effort alongside trust in unseen assistance.
shortened: But the conquest of hearts is difficult, save through the power of the Most Great Name and the hosts ye cannot see. Therefore, strive thou with heart and soul that thou mayest be successful in conquering hearts, and mayest find thy breast expanded, and become the recipient of the outpourings of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Read the account of children’s recitation in its particular voice.
shortened: O you who are firm in the Covenant! Your letter arrived and its contents brought endless joy, for it conveyed the glad tidings of the chanting of verses and recitation of prayers in gatherings of sanctification and teaching, where those who claim knowledge and learning are overcome and brought low before children. This is the power of the Greatest Name that makes the great ones conquered by children and renowned hawks subdued by weak mosquitoes.

order.why: Consider assistance through the Pen.
Read remembrance as an invitation to turn toward God.
shortened: Remind the people of this Most Great Name, that they may become aware and turn unto God, the Peerless, the All-Informed.

order.why: Join seeing, hearing, understanding, and proclaiming.
Keep wise speech that withstands clamor.
shortened: He ariseth amidst mankind and speaketh through the Most Great Name with wisdom and utterance in such wise that the clamor of the heedless shall not silence him.

order.why: Read the call continuing amid imprisonment.
shortened: Despite His imprisonment and tribulation, He summoneth the world through His Most Great Name with a power that the might of the oppressors hath failed to withhold.

order.why: Turn remembrance into action.
shortened: Say: O friends! Break the chains of the utterances of the wicked through the power of the Most Great Name and arise to action.

order.why: Connect receiving from the Ocean with arising among peoples.
shortened: Blessed is he who takes his portion from the Most Great Ocean and arises amidst the peoples with this Name which God has made the Sovereign of names in the kingdom of creation, and through which He has attracted the hearts of those who believe in His unity.

order.why: Read steadfastness among peoples.
Keep strength sought through refuge.
shortened: Seek thou shelter in the Greatest Name, and appear in the utmost strength and power.

order.why: Retain the counsel to firmness in every condition.
shortened: O friends! Through the power of the Most Great Name, remain firm and steadfast on the Most Straight Path, and in all conditions take refuge in the Truth.

order.why: Preserve the source omission in the account of names’ influence.
Read the handmaidens’ recognition and thanksgiving.
Close the linked readings with offering the waters of life freely.
Conclude with the supplied letter’s explanation of the ringstone’s three planes.

questions: What makes a name more than a familiar sound or visible inscription in these passages?
How do the readings relate invocation of the Name to recognition of Baha’u’llah?
What questions does the ringstone’s depiction of God, revelation, and creation invite about mediation and spiritual knowledge?
How does comparison with the Qur’anic passage on beautiful names illuminate both shared devotional themes and distinctive meanings?
What do the prayers seek to change in the person who prays, and how do their images of healing and protection function?
How might daily remembrance become a source of generosity, wise speech, and steadfast action?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 7:180 · Invoking the beautiful names
references.note: Read the invitation to call upon God through the beautiful names, alongside the warning about their misuse. Compare this devotional setting with remembrance, recognition, and the meanings of the Greatest Name in the compilation. The shared theme of sacred naming leaves room to examine the distinctive theological claims of each text.

subjects.displayTitle: East and West: learning to meet as one human family
subjects.introduction: Each point on the earth, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, is east of one place and west of another, so the two words that seem to divide the world name nothing fixed. What they do name is a longing: that East and West might embrace like two lovers, assist one another, and find in each other’s company comfort rather than suspicion. His own journey across the ocean was made for that purpose, and small scenes give the longing a body: a gathering on board ship, letters crossing between assemblies, schools built with help from both sides, a Persian poetess translating an American poem. Alongside the tenderness stand hard historical judgements about religion rising in the East and civilization flourishing in the West, about domination, condescension and reversed fortunes; they belong to particular speakers and moments, and one human family is the measure for weighing them. The Qur’an says that peoples and tribes were made so that they might know one another, with honor measured by righteousness rather than origin [1]. From here the way leads into what is praised and criticised in Eastern and Western cultures, the two kinds of civilization, material and spiritual, that each must learn from the other, and the patient work of building community.
subjects.arc: Begin with the relativity of East and West and universal belonging, make encounter tangible through friendship and communication, examine reciprocal learning and historical tensions, then return to peace and shared service.

order.why: Open with East and West as relative directions within one homeland.
shortened: One of my greatest hopes is the connection between East and West, for this is the greatest service to the world of humanity. In reality, there is no East and West - all points on the earth have the same status, and each point is west in relation to one point and east in relation to another point. Therefore these are relative and conventional matters. All points are one sphere and one homeland, and humanity is one race and one family.
Therefore I am very pleased to observe this assembly that is the cause of progress for Easterners and their fellowship and harmony with Westerners.

order.why: Keep the reported challenge to fixed geographical divisions.
Read the universal good cause beyond any region.
Connect one sun, one home, and shared divine mercy.
shortened: Now, praised be God, the light of love hath spread in both East and West, and the tabernacle of fellowship amongst hearts and souls is raised in the midmost heart of the world. The teachings of Baha'u'llah have been spread in the East and the West, the fame of the Kingdom hath encompassed the earth, and the tidings of the world's Great Peace have created tumult in the realm of the hearts.

It is because the East and the West are illumined by the one sun, all races, nations and creeds are the servants of the one God. The whole earth is one home, and all the people are bathed in the ocean of God's mercy.

order.why: Introduce the embrace of two lovers as the central image.
Make mutual assistance explicit.
shortened: Cooperation and mutual assistance are the basis of the religion of God. The East must assist the West and the West must assist the East.

order.why: Read the journey’s aim as each side’s comfort and peace.
Keep the reported wish to remove misunderstandings.
Begin concrete encounter with the shipboard gathering.
Read the public meeting as evidence of possible unity.
Keep the brief report of courteous hospitality.
Read gratitude for a meeting across geographical origins.
Retain the reported meeting’s love and harmony.
shortened: This is indeed a blessed meeting, for the East and the West are joined here in love and harmony. This was the Will of the Blessed Perfection."

order.why: Keep the Theosophical gathering’s spiritual explanation.
Read the reported assembly of Eastern and Western people.
Recounts finding spiritual aspiration in the West and calls for wider sharing of Eastern teachings.
Consider the banquet as a tangible connection.
shortened: The holding of meetings at which people from the East come to the far West and sit together with you with such love and affection was impossible but through His penetrative power Baha'u'llah has made this easy and has joined the East and the West.

order.why: Read the meeting for students from many countries.
shortened: An especial meeting was held in Mrs Whyte's house for the Oriental students. They were from China, Japan, Persia, India Turkey, Syria, Arabia, Turkey, etc. It was a wonderful demonstration of the union of the East and of the West.

order.why: Consider marriages as examples of relationship.
Keep the personal wish for lasting physical and spiritual union.
Read the account of sacrifice for someone from another region.
shortened: Consider what a difference exists between his country and thine and what a great effect this Bahai spirit hath manifested that an Oriental sacrificeth his life for an Occidental!

order.why: Consider the reported transformation of attitudes toward shared vessels.
Balance hospitality with the reported consequences of mistreating attendants.
shortened: Since the people of the East have not treated the attendants of this ship well, they now look upon those people with contempt.

order.why: Read the encounter between former wartime enemies.
shortened: See! the Americans and the Germans have been hostile and yet how the Germans, are receiving the Americans! This is because they arc the lovers of the Holy Cause, and its principles, striving for the fulfilment of its great purpose. National prejudices cannot interfere in their religion.

order.why: Preserve the particular question about considerate reception.
Keep the question about Persians and Americans in Dublin.
Read the request for a Tablet as an act of cross-regional remembrance.
Consider friends holding distant friends in mind.
shortened: It is through the grace of the Divine Unity that the friends of the East are occupied with thoughts of the friends of the West, and the beloved ones of the South are intimate with the faithful ones of the North.

order.why: Keep the reported remembrance of the East while in the West.
shortened: During this period, although I was in the West, my face was always turned towards the friends in the East, and I would beseech confirmation for them from the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Read the ocean crossed through affection and spiritual communication.
shortened: O friends of this yearning one! Though the distance is great and the boundless ocean lies between us, you are companions and confidants, friends and intimates. For the power of the Word of God has brought the far near and made distant spaces close. East and West have become as one gathering, as one feast adorned.

order.why: Consider the earth as one gathering.
shortened: Therefore we are intimate companions and confidants, of one breath and one voice. The power of the Abha Kingdom has established connection - East has embraced West, distant regions have drawn near, the face of the earth has taken on the character of a single gathering.

order.why: Keep strangers becoming friends.
Move from personal ties to communication among assemblies.
Read correspondence as a means of drawing hearts together.
shortened: The correspondence of the believers of God with all parts of America and from America to all directions is very acceptable and seasonable. It will be the means of drawing the hearts together. Unquestionably show ye the utmost of effort in this matter and correspond with every part.

order.why: Keep the reciprocal communication with all parts of the world.
Consider the enkindling effect of letters.
Read enthusiasm and joy on both sides.
shortened: Regarding what thou wrote about correspondence between East and West - this is very beneficial and causes enthusiasm and joy on both sides.

order.why: Retain the particular invitation to correspond.
shortened: I hope that thou wilt correspond and communicate with them so that a divine connection and heavenly relationship may be established between the East and the West.

order.why: Preserve the source omission in the received message.
Read correspondence as learning one another’s methods.
Make visits and sharing news with isolated places concrete.
shortened: Even travelling and passing through these foreign lands is beneficial, for there are some places so isolated from others that the friends do not receive news from anywhere. If they hear any reports it is by accident. subjects.displayTitle: Science and religion: inquiry with the whole mind
subjects.introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once told an audience to weigh his own words against science and reason and to reject them if they failed the test. Few teachers have handed their listeners so sharp a knife, and the gesture says what harmony of science and religion means in his hands: not a truce between two authorities but a single reality seen from two sides, like a bird that needs both wings or two circles drawn about one centre. Religion without reason sinks into superstition; science without the heart hardens into a materialism that has learned to kill efficiently. The demand cuts both ways, and it leaves work to do. Inherited dogma must be sifted from the spiritual law it has overgrown, and a scientific fact distinguished from the theory of the hour, while the long building of a civilization in which learning and conscience grow together requires patience with unresolved questions. Emerson, insisting that thought is devout and devotion is thought, keeps that aspiration company from another tradition [1]. The road continues into the independent investigation of truth, the mind’s power of discovery, and the difference between sight and insight.
subjects.arc: Begin with the invitation to test the speaker’s words, examine the unity of truth and the work of reason, explore interpretation and changing knowledge, then consider moral purpose and the closing letters on patient inquiry.

order.why: Read the rejection of claims that violate reason.
Ask how sacred texts can be understood without reason.
shortened: Thanks be to God, that in this new cycle the admonition of Baha'u'llah is that in the search for truth man must weigh religious questions in the balance of science and reason. God has given us rational minds for this purpose, to penetrate all things, to find truth. If one renounce reason, what remains? The sacred texts? How can we understand God's commands and to what use can we put them without the balance of reason?

order.why: Open with the invitation to weigh even the speaker’s own words.
shortened: But you must weigh these words of mine against science and reason. If they accord with these, accept them; if not, reject them. For in the human world there is no greater gift than reason. Reason discovers the realities of things. Reason is the standard of understanding.

Keep the challenge of scientific disagreement explicit.
shortened: Between scientists and the followers of religion there has always been controversy and strife for the reason that the latter have proclaimed religion superior in authority to science and considered scientific announcement opposed to the teachings of religion. Baha'u'llah declared that religion is in complete harmony with science and reason. If religious belief and doctrine is at variance with reason, it proceeds from the limited mind of man and not from God; therefore, it is unworthy of belief and not deserving of attention; the heart finds no rest in it, and real faith is impossible.

order.why: Consider responsibility when a dogma cannot be believed.

shortened: Religion and science are the two wings upon which man's intelligence can soar into the heights, with which the human soul can progress. It is not possible to fly with one wing alone! Should a man try to fly with the wing of religion alone he would quickly fall into the quagmire of superstition, whilst on the other hand, with the wing of science alone he would also make no progress, but fall into the despairing slough of materialism.

I say unto you: weigh carefully in the balance of reason and science everything that is presented to you as religion. If it passes this test, then accept it, for it is truth! If, however, it does not so conform, then reject it, for it is ignorance!

order.why: Consider the demand for mutual scrutiny.
shortened: Among other principles of Baha'u'llah's teachings was the harmony of science and religion. Religion must stand the analysis of reason. It must agree with scientific fact and proof so that science will sanction religion and religion fortify science. Both are indissolubly welded and joined in reality. If statements and teachings of religion are found to be unreasonable and contrary to science, they are outcomes of superstition and imagination.

order.why: Read the reciprocal account of true religion and true science.

Consider testing in relation to acquired knowledge.

shortened: Any religious belief which is not conformable with scientific proof and investigation is superstition, for true science is reason and reality, and religion is essentially reality and pure reason; therefore, the two must correspond. Religious teaching which is at variance with science and reason is human invention and imagination unworthy of acceptance, for the antithesis and opposite of knowledge is superstition born of the ignorance of man. If we say religion is opposed to science, we lack knowledge of either true science or true religion, for both are founded upon the premises and conclusions of reason, and both must bear its test.

Therefore religion must accord with science, and if it does not, it is vain imagining and false.

order.why: Keep praise of knowledge in the passage’s religious setting.
shortened: Whereas the religion of God is the promoter of truth, the establisher of science and learning, the supporter of knowledge, the civilizer of the human race, the discoverer of the secrets of existence, and the enlightener of the horizons of the world. How then could it oppose knowledge? God forbid! On the contrary, in the sight of God knowledge is the greatest human virtue and the noblest human perfection.
For knowledge is light, life, felicity, perfection and beauty, and causes the soul to draw nigh to the divine threshold.

order.why: Read discovery alongside spiritual insight.
shortened: Just as human intellects have revealed the secrets of matter and have brought forth from the realm of the invisible the mysteries of nature, may minds and spirits, likewise, come into the knowledge of the verities of God, and the realities of the Kingdom be made manifest in human hearts.

order.why: Preserve the reported affirmation about spiritual science without turning it into medical guidance.

shortened: In the world of existence physical things have a connection with spiritual realities. One of these things is the voice, which connects itself with the spirit; and the spirit can be uplifted by this means -- for though it is a physical thing, it is one of the material, natural organizations -- therefore, it is effective.

order.why: Join the nourishment of the mind to movement of the heart.
shortened: Conversely, the material mind finds various nourishments and progresses through wonderful scientific discoveries.
So if you want to have lofty aspirations, you must set the heart in motion to unite with knowledge - that is, to join spiritual virtues with physical perfections.

order.why: Read material and divine sciences as two wings.
shortened: Scientific knowledge is the highest attainment upon the human plane, for science is the discoverer of realities. It is of two kinds: material and spiritual. Material science is the investigation of natural phenomena; divine science is the discovery and realization of spiritual verities. The world of humanity must acquire both. A bird has two wings; it cannot fly with one. Material and spiritual science are the two wings of human uplift and attainment. Both are necessary -- one the natural, the other supernatural; one material, the other divine.

order.why: Connect material and spiritual progress with peace.

shortened: Morality is the basis of the happiness of the world of humanity. Merciful attributes are the best adornments of man. Science holds the next position to morality.

If a nation be well qualified with education and yet dispossessed of good morals, it will not attain happiness. If that same nation be dispossessed of education, but possessed of moral training, it will be capable of accomplishing philanthropic deeds. When Morality and science go hand in hand, then will it be light upon light.

It is not multiple, there is no difference in any reality. If a religious question be opposed to reason and science, it is pure imagination and baseless, for the opposite of knowledge or science is ignorance.

The first is investigation of truth,
The second, the oneness of mankind,
The third, universal peace,
The fourth, conformity between science and divine revelation,
The fifth, abandonment of racial, religious, worldly and political prejudices, prejudices which destroy the foundation of mankind.

order.why: Keep the links with education, equality, and economic life.
shortened: For every era hath a spirit; the spirit of this illumined era lieth in the teachings of Baha'u'llah. For these lay the foundation of the oneness of the world of humanity and promulgate universal brotherhood. They are founded upon the unity of science and religion and upon investigation of truth. They uphold the principle that religion must be the cause of amity, union and harmony among men. They establish the equality of both sexes and propound economic principles which are for the happiness of individuals. They diffuse universal education, that every soul may as much as possible have a share of knowledge.

order.why: Read the wider social horizon of the teaching.
Retain the reported message on peace and equality.
Keep the reported claim about the conformity of the teachings attributed.
Read the connection with East and West and the overcoming of prejudice.
Follow the speaker’s account of practical aims for society.
Keep the reported hope for the end of European war in its historical setting.
shortened: Therefore when this Cause is fully spread in Europe, warfare will be the thing of the past, universal Peace will be realized, the oneness of the world of humanity will be practiced, religion and science will work hand in hand.

order.why: Retain the interview’s formulation of harmony.
Connect religion and science with peace.
Read love, science, and unity together.
shortened: We hope that the friends of God and handmaidens of the Merciful will, in accordance with heavenly teachings, serve the unity of the human world, consider religion as the foundation of love and fellowship among humanity, and strive to reconcile religion and science.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a wish for clear and convincing speech.
shortened: I desire that all of you may speak on the material and divine sciences with clear and convincing words.

order.why: Begin the supplied readings with the reported unity of religion and reason.
Keep the parallel description of both as light.
Read the supplied fragment on confidence with its omission visible.
Distinguish scientific fact and reasoning from particular conclusions and theories.
Consider the reciprocal implications of studying in the light of revelation and reason.
Keep the cited saying about knowledge’s single point attributed as a hadith.
Retain the provisional astronomical translation and its supplied citation without splicing variants.
Read the Guardian’s characterization of the Revelation in the letter’s own voice.
Consider the account of scientific discovery in the later letter.
Read the full challenge to a rigid separation of faith and reason.
shortened: It has become customary in the West to think of science and religion as occupying two distinct -- and even opposed -- areas of human thought and activity. This dichotomy can be characterized in the pairs of antitheses: faith and reason; value and fact. It is a dichotomy which is foreign to Baha'i thought and should be regarded with suspicion by Baha'i scholars in every field. The principle of the harmony of religion and science means not only that religious teachings should be studied in the light of reason and evidence as well as of faith and inspiration, but also that everything in creation, all aspects of human life and knowledge, should be studied in the light of revelation as well as of purely rational investigation.

order.why: Join moral guidance for applications with impartial testing of religious convictions.
Make room for ambiguity in the long work of building civilization.
shortened: The prosecution of this vast enterprise will depend on a progressive interaction between the truths and principles of religion and the discoveries and insights of scientific inquiry. This entails living with ambiguities as a natural and inescapable feature of the process of exploring reality. It also requires us not to limit science to any particular school of thought or methodological approach postulated in the course of its development.

order.why: Distinguish harmony from confinement to current scientific concepts.
Bring Emerson’s account of thought and devotion into comparative conversation.
shortened: Love is as much its demand, as perception. Indeed, neither can be perfect without the other. In the uttermost meaning of the words, thought is devout, and devotion is thought.

But when a faithful thinker, resolute to detach every object from personal relations, and see it in the light of thought, shall, at the same time, kindle science with the fire of the holiest affections, then will God go forth anew into the creation.

order.why: Keep the supplied discussion of superstition and estrangement in full.
shortened: The unfortunate effect of this is that science has drifted apart from religion, and religion has become a mere blind and more or less apathetic following of the precepts of certain religious teachers, who insist on their own favourite dogmas being accepted even when they are contrary to science. This is foolishness, for it is quite evident that science is the light, and, being so, religion truly so-called does not oppose knowledge.

But the religion which does not walk hand in hand with science is itself in the darkness of superstition and ignorance. Much of the discord and disunion of the world is created by these man-made oppositions and contradictions. If religion were in harmony with science and they walked together, much of the hatred and bitterness now bringing misery to the human race would be at an end.

order.why: Close with the limit on religious sponsorship of scientific treatments.

Compare that aspiration with the call for science and religion to support one another, while examining his distinctive claims about spirit, intuition, and the limits of empirical study.
